# `Q-9-4` — Invalid XML Structure

> The XML document is well-formed at the token level but its
> structure violates a constraint the parser enforces.

## What this means

`Q-9-4` is the catch-all the XML parser uses when the input is
syntactically well-formed (all tags balanced, no stray
characters) but the *structure* breaks an XML rule the parser
cares about — for instance, content appearing where only
declarations are allowed, or a processing instruction outside
its permitted position. The message names the specific
constraint that failed.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **Content before the XML declaration.** `<?xml version="1.0"?>`
  must be the very first thing in the document.
- **A namespace prefix used without being declared.**
- **A construct that is legal XML in general but illegal in the
  position it appears in.**

## How to fix

Read the message — it names the specific constraint. The fix
usually has the same shape as the constraint: move the
declaration earlier, declare the namespace, or remove the
out-of-place construct.

## Related

- `Q-9-1` — generic XML syntax error: lower-level
  well-formedness problems.
